paper.title: POWERPLAY: Training an Increasingly General Problem Solver by Continually Searching for the Simplest Still Unsolvable Problem
paper.central_claim: PowerPlay searches pairs of (new self-invented task, modification of the current solver) until it finds a solver that provably solves all previously learned tasks plus the new one while its predecessor does not; by design it does not forget, and it is claimed to train an increasingly general problem solver. In-scope reading: the program-modifying (OOPS-style) branch; the RNN-weight branch and the externally reported experiments are not harness evidence.

signatures.object: Pair (task T_i, solver s_i) added to a growing repertoire; solver is a program (OOPS/FORTH-like) or an RNN weight matrix.
signatures.information: Search program may read solver code and recorded traces; tasks carry a deterministic solved-check; no external labels in the basic variant.
signatures.operation: Candidate program p invents T, modifies s_{i-1} into q, and demonstrates that q (not s_{i-1}) solves T and still solves all earlier tasks; first validated pair under complexity-ordered search is accepted.
signatures.output: Accepted tuple (i, p_i, s_i, T_i, Trace_i).
signatures.conditions: Computable task checks or replayable traces; verifier exact (or probabilistic variant with stated assumptions); enough search time.
signatures.feedback: Internal task checker and trace replay.
signatures.selection_rule: Strict non-regression + novelty (Variant I); cost decrease > epsilon (Variant II).
signatures.selection_data: The stored repertoire itself; no independent held-out set.
signatures.persistence: Read-only storage of programs, tasks, solvers, traces; rejected candidates undone.
signatures.later_use: Later search programs may read/copy stored code; s_i is the base for step i+1; may seed external tasks (§6).
signatures.claimed_effect: Monotonically growing repertoire without forgetting; increasingly general solver (asserted, not shown here).
signatures.failure_boundary: Greedy myopia, trivial-task modularisation, verification cost, noisy environments need replay/probabilistic variants, safety (§10).

gap.author_gap: Optimal universal solvers are impractical (constant slowdowns) and earlier curiosity systems could forget; need a practical way to keep inventing the simplest still-unsolvable task without losing earlier skills.
gap.checked_gap: Real at the level of design guarantees; its practical size is not measured in this paper.
